extraction.name: CoNLL-2003 named entity data
extraction.description: Language-independent named entity recognition data sets for English and German.
extraction.creator: Erik F. Tjong Kim Sang and Fien De Meulder
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The data was extracted from existing news corpora: the Reuters Corpus for English and the ECI Multilingual Text Corpus for German.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Reuters news stories and German newspaper Frankfurter Rundshau articles.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: August 1996 to August 1997 for English; August to December 1992 for German.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: The raw data was processed using a tokenizer, part-of-speech tagger, and a chunker.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Named entity tagging was done manually following MUC conventions, with an additional MISC category for names not fitting into PER, ORG, or LOC.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, tuning parameters (development), and testing machine learning methods for named entity recognition.

name.evidence: The CoNLL-2003 named entity data consists of eight files covering two languages: English and German

description.evidence: We describe the CoNLL-2003 shared task: language-independent named entity recognition. We give background information on the data sets (English and German)

creator.evidence:

inLanguage.evidence: The CoNLL-2003 named entity data consists of eight files covering two languages: English and German

rai:dataCollection.evidence: The English data was taken from the Reuters Corpus... The text for the German data was taken from the ECI Multilingual Text Corpus

rai:dataCollectionType.evidence: The English data was taken from the Reuters Corpus... The text for the German data was taken from the ECI Multilingual Text Corpus

rai:dataCollectionRawData.evidence: The English data was taken from the Reuters Corpus. This corpus consists of Reuters news stories... The text for the German data was taken from the ECI Multilingual Text Corpus... extracted from the German newspaper Frankfurter Rundshau.

rai:dataCollectionTimeframe.evidence: This corpus consists of Reuters news stories between August 1996 and August 1997... The raw data were taken from the months of September to December 1992.

rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol.evidence: for all data, a tokenizer, part-of-speech tagger, and a chunker were applied to the raw data.

rai:dataAnnotationProtocol.evidence: Named entity tagging of English and German training, development, and test data, was done by hand at the University of Antwerp. Mostly, MUC conventions were followed (Chinchor et al., 1999). An extra named entity category called MISC was added to denote all names which are not already in the other categories.

rai:machineAnnotationTools.evidence: The English data was tagged and chunked by the memory-based MBT tagger (Daelemans et al., 2002). The German data was lemmatized, tagged and chunked by the decision tree tagger Treetagger (Schmid, 1995).

rai:dataUseCases.evidence: The leaming methods were trained with the training data. The development data could be used for tuning the parameters of the leaming methods... When the best parameters were found, the method could be trained on the training data and tested on the test data.
